note: Idea DAG and family split for the problem map. Built by the backbone pass; writers fill content/drafts/pm_<family>.json (see WRITERS.md).

ideas.name: Hash set membership
ideas.summary: Put items in a hash set so that 'have I seen this?' is answered in constant time on average.

ideas.name: Linear scan with running state
ideas.summary: Walk the array once and keep a few variables, such as the current streak or the best so far.

ideas.name: Sort first, then scan neighbours
ideas.summary: Sorting puts related values next to each other, so one pass over neighbours finds what a double loop would.

ideas.name: Walk a linked list with a pointer
ideas.summary: Follow next pointers from the head until null, doing work at each node.

ideas.name: Recursion with a base case
ideas.summary: A function solves a smaller copy of the same problem and stops at a case it can answer directly.

ideas.name: Scan a string character by character
ideas.summary: Treat the string as an array of characters and process each one, using character codes when needed.

ideas.name: Closed-form arithmetic instead of a loop
ideas.summary: Use a formula such as 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2 to replace a loop or a search.

ideas.name: Peel digits with % 10 and / 10
ideas.summary: The last digit is n % 10 and the rest is n // 10, so a loop reads every digit.

ideas.name: Read and set single bits
ideas.summary: Use &, |, ^, << and >> to test, set, clear and count the bits of an integer.

ideas.name: Walk a 2-D grid by row and column
ideas.summary: Index cells as grid[r][c] with nested loops; cells on one diagonal share r - c, on one anti-diagonal r + c.

ideas.name: Simulate the rules step by step
ideas.summary: Do exactly what the statement says, step by step, after checking that the number of steps is small enough.

ideas.name: Closures and higher-order functions
ideas.summary: A function can return another function that remembers the variables of the call that made it.

ideas.name: Frequency counting
ideas.summary: Count how many times each value appears, in a hash map or a small fixed array, and compare or query the counts.

ideas.name: Sort with a custom key or comparator
ideas.summary: Define what 'smaller' means for your items, then let the library sort do the work.

ideas.name: Divide and conquer
ideas.summary: Split the input into parts, solve each part recursively, and combine the parts' answers.

ideas.name: Brute-force enumeration over a small space
ideas.summary: When the input is small, try every candidate directly; check the constraints to see that the loop count is affordable.

ideas.name: Hash map from key to index or value
ideas.summary: Store each value with the data you need later, so the matching partner is found in one lookup.

ideas.name: Use the array itself as a hash table
ideas.summary: When values lie in 1..n, mark value v at index v-1 (by sign or by swapping it home) to get O(1) extra space.

ideas.name: Majority vote by cancellation
ideas.summary: Pair off different values against each other; a value that appears more than half the time survives the cancelling.

ideas.name: Prefix sums for range totals
ideas.summary: Store running totals once so the sum of any range is the difference of two stored totals.

ideas.name: Fixed-size sliding window
ideas.summary: Slide a window of size k: add the item entering on the right and remove the item leaving on the left.

ideas.name: Merge two sorted sequences
ideas.summary: Walk two sorted lists with one pointer each and always take the smaller head.

ideas.name: Match a subsequence with one pointer per string
ideas.summary: Advance through the long string and move the short string's pointer only when the characters match.

ideas.name: Two pointers from both ends
ideas.summary: Start one index at each end and move them toward each other, comparing or combining the two items.

ideas.name: Read and write pointers to filter in place
ideas.summary: One index reads every item and a slower one writes only the items you keep, so the array is edited in place.

ideas.name: Dummy head node to simplify edits
ideas.summary: Put a fake node before the head so removing or inserting at the front is no special case.

ideas.name: Fast and slow pointers
ideas.summary: Move one pointer two steps and one pointer one step; they meet if there is a cycle, and the slow one stops at the middle.

ideas.name: Reverse links in place
ideas.summary: Walk the list and point each node back at the previous one, keeping three pointers.

ideas.name: Queue for first-in first-out order
ideas.summary: Add at the back and remove from the front, so items are handled in arrival order.

ideas.name: Stack for last-in first-out matching
ideas.summary: Push openers and pop when a closer arrives; with one kind of bracket a depth counter is enough.

ideas.name: Binary search on a sorted array
ideas.summary: Compare with the middle item and keep only the half that can still contain the target (also when you can only ask a hidden judge).

ideas.name: Preorder, inorder and postorder
ideas.summary: Visit a node before, between or after its subtrees; each order suits a different kind of question.

ideas.name: Recursion on a binary tree
ideas.summary: Solve the left and right subtrees, then combine their answers at the node.

ideas.name: Greedy: take the locally best choice
ideas.summary: Make the choice that looks best now and never undo it, after checking that this cannot lose the optimum.

ideas.name: Min-heap / priority queue
ideas.summary: A heap gives the smallest (or largest) item in O(1) and adds or removes items in O(log n).

ideas.name: Sort intervals by start and merge
ideas.summary: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are neighbours, so one pass merges or checks them.

ideas.name: Generate subsets by include or exclude
ideas.summary: At each item, branch on taking it or not; the leaves of this tree are all 2^n subsets.

ideas.name: Grade-school arithmetic on digit strings
ideas.summary: Add or multiply numbers stored as strings digit by digit from the right, carrying as on paper.

ideas.name: Finite-state machine parsing
ideas.summary: Keep a current state and move between states on each character class, which keeps edge cases explicit.

ideas.name: Build strings with a buffer
ideas.summary: Append pieces to a list or builder and join once, because repeated string concatenation copies every time.

ideas.name: Compare strings character by character
ideas.summary: Walk two or more strings in step to find where they first differ, which also defines their order.

ideas.name: Split into tokens and join
ideas.summary: Cut the text into words or fields at separators, work on the tokens, then join them back.

ideas.name: Convert between number bases
ideas.summary: Repeatedly divide by the base and collect remainders, or multiply and add to go back.

ideas.name: Count with binomial coefficients
ideas.summary: Count choices with C(n, k), built from Pascal's rule C(n, k) = C(n-1, k-1) + C(n-1, k) or a formula.

ideas.name: Trial division up to the square root
ideas.summary: Any composite n has a factor at most sqrt(n), so trial division up to sqrt(n) finds the prime factors.

ideas.name: Euclid's GCD and LCM
ideas.summary: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) shrinks fast, and lcm(a, b) = a / gcd(a, b) * b.

ideas.name: Points, distances and cross products
ideas.summary: Use integer cross products for direction and collinearity and squared distances to avoid square roots.

ideas.name: Invariant and parity arguments
ideas.summary: Find a quantity that never changes, or only changes in a known way, and reason from it instead of simulating.

ideas.name: Modular arithmetic for large counts
ideas.summary: Take results mod a prime such as 1e9+7 after each addition and multiplication so numbers stay small.

ideas.name: Rejection sampling
ideas.summary: Draw from a bigger uniform range and retry when the draw falls outside a range that divides evenly.

ideas.name: Reservoir sampling
ideas.summary: Keep the i-th item with probability 1/i, so after any number of items each one was kept with equal chance.

ideas.name: Fisher–Yates shuffle
ideas.summary: Swap each position with a random position at or after it, which makes every order equally likely.

ideas.name: Arithmetic with bit operations
ideas.summary: Addition is XOR for the sum bits plus AND shifted left for the carries, repeated until no carry is left.

ideas.name: Lowest set bit tricks
ideas.summary: x & (x - 1) clears the lowest set bit and x & -x keeps only it.

ideas.name: A bitmask as a small set
ideas.summary: Store a set of up to about 30 items (such as letters) in one integer, so union and intersection are single operations.

ideas.name: XOR cancels pairs
ideas.summary: x ^ x = 0 and x ^ 0 = x, so XOR-ing everything leaves only the value without a partner.

ideas.name: Date and time arithmetic
ideas.summary: Count days with month lengths and leap-year rules, or convert times to minutes since midnight.

ideas.name: Direction arrays for moving on a grid
ideas.summary: List the moves as (dr, dc) pairs and loop over them, checking bounds, instead of writing each move by hand.

ideas.name: Store old and new state in one cell
ideas.summary: Keep the next state in spare bits (or the first row and column as markers) so the update needs no copy.

ideas.name: Rotate or flip a matrix in place
ideas.summary: A 90-degree rotation is a transpose followed by reversing each row.

ideas.name: Walk a matrix in spiral order
ideas.summary: Keep top, bottom, left and right bounds and shrink one bound after each side is walked.

ideas.name: Promises, timers and async control
ideas.summary: A promise stands for a value that arrives later; timers and await order work without blocking the thread.

ideas.name: Walk nested objects and arrays
ideas.summary: Recurse into values that are arrays or objects, handling each type, to flatten, compare or copy them.

ideas.name: Counting sort for small value ranges
ideas.summary: When values are small integers, count each value and read the counts in order instead of comparing items.

ideas.name: Merge sort
ideas.summary: Sort each half recursively and merge the two sorted halves in linear time, for O(n log n) overall.

ideas.name: Count pairs with a running count map
ideas.summary: Count pairs i < j by adding, at each j, how many earlier items match it according to the count map.

ideas.name: Group by a canonical key
ideas.summary: Turn each item into a key that equal items share (sorted letters, a count tuple) and group items by that key.

ideas.name: Coordinate compression
ideas.summary: Replace large or sparse values by their rank among the sorted distinct values, so arrays can be indexed by them.

ideas.name: Difference array for range updates
ideas.summary: Add +v where a range starts and -v after it ends, then one prefix sum gives every position's final value.

ideas.name: 2-D prefix sums
ideas.summary: Store sums of top-left rectangles so any rectangle sum is four lookups combined by inclusion and exclusion.

ideas.name: Prefix sum plus hash map of earlier totals
ideas.summary: A subarray sums to k when two prefix totals differ by k, so count earlier totals in a hash map.

ideas.name: Prefix and suffix aggregates (left and right passes)
ideas.summary: Compute what lies to the left and to the right of every index in two passes, then combine them per index.

ideas.name: Fixed window compared by counts
ideas.summary: Keep the letter counts of the window and update them by one letter in and one out as it slides.

ideas.name: Move the pointer that cannot improve the answer
ideas.summary: At each step one end is provably useless for any better answer, so drop it and keep a linear scan.

ideas.name: Three-way partition (Dutch national flag)
ideas.summary: Keep three regions (less, equal, greater) with three pointers and swap each item into its region in one pass.

ideas.name: Two pointers on a sorted array for a target sum
ideas.summary: If the pair sum is too small move the left pointer up, if too large move the right pointer down.

ideas.name: Variable window: grow right, shrink left while invalid
ideas.summary: Extend the right end every step and move the left end only as far as needed to make the window valid again.

ideas.name: Map old nodes to new nodes
ideas.summary: Copy each node once and use a map (or interleaved copies) to wire the copies' extra pointers.

ideas.name: Find where a cycle starts (Floyd)
ideas.summary: After the pointers meet, restart one from the head; moving both one step at a time, they meet at the cycle's entry.

ideas.name: Doubly linked list with sentinels
ideas.summary: Give each node prev and next pointers and keep head and tail sentinels, so any known node is removed in O(1).

ideas.name: Merge sorted linked lists
ideas.summary: Attach the smaller head to a growing tail, starting from a dummy node.

ideas.name: Cut, reverse and re-link list segments
ideas.summary: Find a split point, reverse a part in place, and stitch the pieces back together.

ideas.name: Stack that also tracks the minimum
ideas.summary: Store, with each pushed item, the minimum of the stack at that moment, so the minimum is always on top.

ideas.name: Monotonic stack for next greater or smaller element
ideas.summary: Keep a stack of items still waiting for a bigger one; each new item pops and answers everything it beats.

ideas.name: Stack of frames for nested structure
ideas.summary: Save the outer state on a stack when a nested part opens and restore it when the part closes.

ideas.name: Evaluate postfix expressions with a stack
ideas.summary: Push numbers; on an operator pop two numbers, apply it, and push the result.

ideas.name: Stack for cancelling neighbours
ideas.summary: Push each item and let it cancel or merge with the top of the stack, as in collisions or adjacent duplicates.

ideas.name: Find the first index where a condition turns true
ideas.summary: Search for the boundary between false and true (lower bound) instead of an exact value.

ideas.name: Search a sorted matrix
ideas.summary: Treat a row-sorted matrix as one sorted array, or walk a staircase from a corner.

ideas.name: Use BST order to choose a side
ideas.summary: In a binary search tree, smaller keys are on the left, so each comparison discards a subtree.

ideas.name: Level-order traversal with a queue
ideas.summary: Process the tree one level at a time by taking exactly the queue's current length each round.

ideas.name: Serialize a tree and read it back
ideas.summary: Write the tree as text in a fixed traversal order, marking empty children, so it can be rebuilt exactly.

ideas.name: Build a balanced tree from sorted data
ideas.summary: Take the middle item as the root and build both halves recursively.

ideas.name: Pass state down the tree
ideas.summary: Carry information from the root downward, such as a running sum or allowed bounds, as extra arguments.

ideas.name: Rebuild a tree from traversal orders
ideas.summary: Preorder gives the root, and its position in the inorder list splits the remaining nodes into left and right.

ideas.name: Iterative traversal with an explicit stack
ideas.summary: Replace the call stack with your own stack of nodes to walk the tree without recursion.

ideas.name: Return several values up the tree
ideas.summary: Each call returns what the parent needs (such as height) while updating a global best (such as the longest path).

ideas.name: Recurse on two trees at once
ideas.summary: Walk both trees in step and compare or merge the matching nodes.

ideas.name: Build an adjacency list from edges
ideas.summary: For each edge, append each end to the other's neighbour list so neighbours are found without scanning all edges.

ideas.name: BFS for fewest steps
ideas.summary: Explore in rings of equal distance with a queue; the first time you reach a cell is by a shortest path.

ideas.name: Flood fill a grid region
ideas.summary: From a start cell, spread to every connected cell of the same kind with DFS or BFS.

ideas.name: Arrange by count with a cooldown
ideas.summary: Always place the most frequent remaining item that is allowed now, or count idle slots from the top frequency.

ideas.name: Event-driven simulation ordered by time
ideas.summary: Keep pending events in a heap by time and process them in order, advancing the clock to the next event.

ideas.name: Sort by a key proved by an exchange argument
ideas.summary: Show that swapping two neighbours out of key order never helps, so sorting by that key is optimal.

ideas.name: Repeatedly combine the two smallest
ideas.summary: Merging the two cheapest items first minimises the total merge cost, as in Huffman coding.

ideas.name: K-way merge with a heap
ideas.summary: Keep the current head of each sorted list in a heap and repeatedly take the smallest.

ideas.name: Lazy deletion from a heap
ideas.summary: Mark items as stale instead of removing them, and throw stale items away when they reach the top.

ideas.name: Track the farthest reach
ideas.summary: Scan left to right keeping the farthest index you can reach; you are stuck if you pass it.

ideas.name: Greedy with take-back (regret heap)
ideas.summary: Commit greedily but keep past choices in a heap, and swap the worst one out when a better use appears.

ideas.name: Restart when the running total goes negative
ideas.summary: If the running balance from a start goes negative, no position in between can be a valid start either.

ideas.name: Count overlaps with a heap of end times
ideas.summary: Sort by start; the heap holds end times of busy rooms, and a room is reused when its end is not after the new start.

ideas.name: Keep a size-k heap for the top k
ideas.summary: Keep the k best seen so far in a min-heap; its top is the k-th best.

ideas.name: Two heaps for a running median
ideas.summary: A max-heap holds the lower half and a min-heap the upper half; balance their sizes after each insert.

ideas.name: Unlock options by sorting, pick the best with a heap
ideas.summary: Add options to a heap as they become available in sorted order and always take the best available one.

ideas.name: Choose items with a start index
ideas.summary: Only pick items after the last one picked, so each combination is generated once.

ideas.name: Generate permutations with a used mark
ideas.summary: At each position, try every unused item, mark it, recurse, and unmark it on the way back.

ideas.name: Memoise a recursion (top-down DP)
ideas.summary: Cache each subproblem's answer the first time it is computed so overlapping calls cost nothing.

ideas.name: Expand around each centre for palindromes
ideas.summary: Every palindrome has a centre, so grow outward from each of the 2n-1 centres while the ends match.

ideas.name: Check a pattern at every start
ideas.summary: Try the pattern at each position and stop at the first mismatch; O(n*m) in the worst case.

ideas.name: Run-length and length-prefixed encoding
ideas.summary: Write each run as a character and a count, or each item as its length plus content, so it decodes without ambiguity.

ideas.name: Trie (prefix tree)
ideas.summary: Store words letter by letter along tree paths, so all words with a prefix share one path.

ideas.name: Fast exponentiation by squaring
ideas.summary: Square the base and halve the exponent, multiplying in the base when the current exponent bit is 1.

ideas.name: Inclusion–exclusion
ideas.summary: Count a union by adding single sets, subtracting pairwise overlaps, adding triple overlaps, and so on.

ideas.name: Winning and losing positions
ideas.summary: A position is losing if every move leads to a winning position; find the pattern of losing positions.

ideas.name: k-th permutation by factorials
ideas.summary: Each first item covers (n-1)! permutations, so divide k by factorials to pick items one by one.

ideas.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
ideas.summary: Cross out the multiples of each prime from p*p up; whatever stays uncrossed is prime.

ideas.name: Hash reduced slopes
ideas.summary: Store each direction as (dy, dx) divided by their gcd with a fixed sign, so equal slopes get equal keys.

ideas.name: Enumerate subsets with a bitmask
ideas.summary: Loop mask from 0 to 2^n - 1 and read which items are in the subset from its bits.

ideas.name: Decide or count bit by bit
ideas.summary: Treat each of the 32 bit positions separately, counting how many numbers have that bit set.

ideas.name: Prefix XOR
ideas.summary: The XOR of a range is the XOR of two prefix XORs, just like range sums.

ideas.name: Split values by a differing bit
ideas.summary: Any set bit of a ^ b separates a from b, so XOR each group separately.

ideas.name: Design a class with state and methods
ideas.summary: Keep the state in fields and make each method update or read it in the required time.

ideas.name: Fenwick tree (binary indexed tree)
ideas.summary: Index i stores the sum of a block whose length is i's lowest set bit, giving prefix sums with updates in O(log n).

ideas.name: Array plus hash map for O(1) random access
ideas.summary: Keep values in an array for random picks and their indexes in a map; delete by swapping with the last item.

ideas.name: Segment tree with point updates
ideas.summary: Each node stores a summary of one range; a query or update touches O(log n) nodes.

ideas.name: Skip list
ideas.summary: Stack sorted linked lists of random heights so a search skips ahead on high levels: O(log n) expected.

ideas.name: Simulate until the state repeats
ideas.summary: Store each state when first seen; when one repeats, jump ahead by whole cycles and finish the remainder.

ideas.name: Table operations (filter, group, join)
ideas.summary: Express the task as selection, projection, grouping and joins over tables instead of loops.

ideas.name: Debounce and throttle
ideas.summary: Delay or drop calls with timers so a function runs at most once per burst or per time slot.

ideas.name: Bucket by value range (pigeonhole)
ideas.summary: Spread values into buckets of a chosen width so the answer can only lie between buckets, not inside one.

ideas.name: Count pairs during the merge step
ideas.summary: While merging two sorted halves, count how many items of the right half beat each item of the left half.

ideas.name: Prefix sums modulo k
ideas.summary: Two prefix totals with the same remainder mod k bound a subarray whose sum is divisible by k.

ideas.name: Line sweep over sorted events
ideas.summary: Turn intervals into start and end events, sort them by position, and keep a running count while walking through them.

ideas.name: Exactly k = at most k minus at most k-1
ideas.summary: Counting windows with exactly k is hard to slide, but counting windows with at most k is easy, so subtract two such counts.

ideas.name: Fix one item, two-pointer the rest (k-sum)
ideas.summary: Sort, fix the first item in a loop, and solve the remaining pair with two pointers, skipping duplicates.

ideas.name: Shortest window that covers all needs
ideas.summary: Grow until every need is met, then shrink from the left while it still holds, recording the shortest valid window.

ideas.name: Parse infix expressions (precedence, parentheses)
ideas.summary: Keep pending numbers and operators on stacks and apply an operator only when a lower-precedence one or a ')' arrives.

ideas.name: Monotonic stack for the smallest sequence
ideas.summary: Pop a larger earlier item whenever a smaller one arrives and removals are still allowed, giving the lexicographically smallest result.

ideas.name: Pop to find each bar's widest span
ideas.summary: When a bar is popped, the bar below it and the bar that popped it are its nearest smaller neighbours, which fixes its width.

ideas.name: Monotonic deque for sliding-window max or min
ideas.summary: Keep candidates in a deque in decreasing order, dropping those that leave the window or can never win again.

ideas.name: Binary search a partition across two arrays
ideas.summary: Binary search how many items to take from the first array so the two left parts together form the lower half.

ideas.name: Binary search on the answer
ideas.summary: When 'is x big enough?' is false then true as x grows, binary search over x instead of over an array.

ideas.name: Binary search by slope (peaks)
ideas.summary: If the next item is larger, a peak lies to the right; otherwise it lies at or to the left.

ideas.name: Binary search on a rotated array
ideas.summary: Compare the middle with an end to learn which half is sorted, then keep the half that holds the answer.

ideas.name: Insert into and delete from a BST
ideas.summary: Walk down to the right place; to delete a node with two children, replace it by its successor.

ideas.name: Inorder of a BST is sorted
ideas.summary: An inorder walk of a BST yields keys in sorted order, so sorted-array tricks apply while walking.

ideas.name: Lowest common ancestor by recursion
ideas.summary: The lowest common ancestor is the first node where the two targets fall into different subtrees.

ideas.name: Morris traversal in O(1) space
ideas.summary: Temporarily link each node's inorder predecessor back to it, so the walk needs no stack, then undo the links.

ideas.name: Treat a tree as a graph to move upward
ideas.summary: Record each node's parent so a BFS can move up as well as down.

ideas.name: Hash each subtree's shape
ideas.summary: Give each subtree a key built from its value and its children's keys, so equal subtrees get equal keys.

ideas.name: DFS on a graph with a visited set
ideas.summary: Visit a node, mark it, and recurse into unmarked neighbours, so each node and edge is handled once.

ideas.name: Count in-degrees and out-degrees
ideas.summary: Many questions about who points to whom are answered by counting incoming and outgoing edges.

ideas.name: Multi-source BFS
ideas.summary: Put every source in the queue at distance 0, so the BFS gives each cell its distance to the nearest source.

ideas.name: BFS over states (implicit graph)
ideas.summary: When nodes are configurations, generate neighbours on the fly and keep a visited set of states.

ideas.name: Union–find with path compression
ideas.summary: Keep a parent pointer per item, join sets by linking roots, and flatten paths on lookup for near-constant time.

ideas.name: Dijkstra with a min-heap
ideas.summary: Always settle the unsettled node with the smallest known distance, relaxing its edges; needs non-negative weights.

ideas.name: Sort by end to keep the most intervals
ideas.summary: Always keep the interval that ends first; it leaves the most room for the rest.

ideas.name: Quickselect partition for the k-th item
ideas.summary: Partition around a random pivot and recurse only into the side that holds position k: O(n) on average.

ideas.name: Skip duplicates after sorting
ideas.summary: Sort, then at one recursion level skip an item equal to the previous one so equal branches are not repeated.

ideas.name: Backtrack on a grid path
ideas.summary: Mark a cell while it is on the current path and unmark it when you return, so other paths may use it.

ideas.name: Meet in the middle
ideas.summary: Enumerate all subsets of each half (2^(n/2) each), sort one side, and combine with binary search.

ideas.name: Place items with conflict sets
ideas.summary: Keep sets of used rows, columns or diagonals so each placement is checked in O(1).

ideas.name: Prune branches that cannot succeed
ideas.summary: Check constraints as early as possible and stop a branch the moment it can no longer lead to a valid answer.

ideas.name: Split a string into valid pieces
ideas.summary: Choose where the next piece ends, check that piece, and recurse on the rest.

ideas.name: 1-D DP table built bottom-up
ideas.summary: Define dp[i] from a few smaller indexes and fill the table from small i to large i.

ideas.name: DP over subsets as bitmasks
ideas.summary: Use an integer's bits as the set of items used so far and memoise on that integer.

ideas.name: Digit DP
ideas.summary: Build numbers digit by digit with a 'still equal to the limit so far' flag to count numbers up to N with a property.

ideas.name: Minimax DP for two-player games
ideas.summary: A position's value is the best move's result assuming the opponent then plays their best.

ideas.name: Rolling hash (Rabin–Karp)
ideas.summary: Hash each window from the previous window's hash in O(1), and compare hashes before comparing text.

ideas.name: Z-function
ideas.summary: For each position, store how long the string matches its own prefix there, reusing the rightmost match box.

ideas.name: Count structures by splitting (Catalan)
ideas.summary: Choose the root or first split, multiply the counts of the two sides, and sum over all choices.

ideas.name: Convex hull (monotone chain)
ideas.summary: Sort points and keep a stack that pops any point that would make a clockwise turn, for each half of the hull.

ideas.name: Modular inverse for nCk mod p
ideas.summary: Divide mod a prime p by multiplying by a^(p-2) (Fermat), so factorial formulas work under the modulus.

ideas.name: Loop over multiples (harmonic bound)
ideas.summary: For each d, visiting its multiples d, 2d, 3d... costs n/d, so all d together cost only n log n.

ideas.name: Weighted random pick
ideas.summary: Draw a number below the total weight and binary search the prefix sums to find whose range it falls in.

ideas.name: Prefix parity mask plus hash map
ideas.summary: Keep a bit per letter that flips on each occurrence; equal masks at two indexes mean even counts between them.

ideas.name: Binary trie to maximise XOR
ideas.summary: Insert numbers bit by bit from the top; to maximise XOR, follow the opposite bit whenever possible.

ideas.name: Iterators with peek and lazy flattening
ideas.summary: Produce items one at a time on request, keeping a look-ahead item or a stack of positions (a BST iterator keeps the left spine).

ideas.name: LRU cache
ideas.summary: A hash map finds nodes and a doubly linked list keeps them in recency order, so get and put are O(1).

ideas.name: Ordered set / sorted map
ideas.summary: A balanced search tree keeps keys sorted under inserts, so floor, ceiling and rank queries take O(log n).

ideas.name: Count smaller items with a Fenwick tree over ranks
ideas.summary: Compress values to ranks, scan, and query how many ranks below the current one were already added.

ideas.name: Lazy propagation for range updates
ideas.summary: Store a pending update on a node and push it to the children only when they are visited.

ideas.name: Segment tree with merged summaries
ideas.summary: Store several values per node (prefix run, suffix run, best run) so two children combine in O(1).

ideas.name: Versioned map with binary search
ideas.summary: Keep each key's history in time order and binary search it for the latest value at or before a given time.

ideas.name: Count events in a time window
ideas.summary: Keep recent timestamps in a queue (or buckets) and drop those older than the window before answering.

ideas.name: Order threads with locks and semaphores
ideas.summary: Make each thread wait on a semaphore or condition that the previous step signals, so prints come in order.

ideas.name: Sweep with an active set (heap or ordered set)
ideas.summary: While sweeping, keep the currently open items in a heap or ordered set so the best open item is always known.

ideas.name: Count each element's share over all subarrays
ideas.summary: An element is the minimum of (left span) x (right span) subarrays, so sum value x count over elements instead of over subarrays.

ideas.name: Binary search with a greedy feasibility check
ideas.summary: Guess a limit, check it with one greedy pass, and binary search for the smallest limit that passes.

ideas.name: Binary search the k-th value by counting
ideas.summary: Guess a value, count how many items are at most it, and binary search for the value whose count reaches k.

ideas.name: Binary search on real numbers
ideas.summary: Bisect a real interval a fixed number of times, or until it is smaller than the required precision.

ideas.name: Bidirectional BFS
ideas.summary: Search from both ends and stop when the frontiers meet, which explores far fewer states.

ideas.name: Two-colouring (bipartite check)
ideas.summary: Colour neighbours with opposite colours; a conflict means an odd cycle and no valid split.

ideas.name: Count connected components
ideas.summary: Start a new search from every unvisited node; the number of starts is the number of components.

ideas.name: Cycle detection in a directed graph
ideas.summary: Mark nodes white, grey (on the current path) or black (done); reaching a grey node means a cycle.

ideas.name: Topological sort (Kahn's algorithm)
ideas.summary: Repeatedly take a node with no remaining prerequisites; if some nodes are never taken, there is a cycle.

ideas.name: Union by shared key
ideas.summary: Join items that share a key (an email, an equal sign, a common factor) and read the groups at the end.

ideas.name: Sort queries offline and union in order
ideas.summary: Sort edges and queries by limit, add edges up to each query's limit, and answer with a find.

ideas.name: Reverse time so deletions become unions
ideas.summary: Union-find cannot split sets, so apply all deletions first and add items back in reverse order.

ideas.name: Weighted union–find
ideas.summary: Store with each parent link a ratio or offset to the parent, and combine them along the path.

ideas.name: Bellman–Ford: relax edges k times
ideas.summary: After k rounds of relaxing every edge, each distance is the best using at most k edges; negative weights are allowed.

ideas.name: Binary lifting for k-th ancestor and LCA
ideas.summary: Store each node's 2^j-th ancestor; any jump of k levels is a few such jumps, one per set bit of k.

ideas.name: Shortest paths over (node, extra state)
ideas.summary: Add the extra resource (time used, stops, keys held) to the node, and run the search on these pairs.

ideas.name: Eulerian path (Hierholzer)
ideas.summary: Use every edge once by DFS that records a node only after all its edges are used, then reverse the record.

ideas.name: Euler tour: a subtree is a range
ideas.summary: Number nodes by DFS entry time; each subtree then covers one contiguous range of numbers.

ideas.name: Floyd–Warshall all-pairs shortest paths
ideas.summary: For each middle node k, improve every distance i->j by going through k; O(n^3) for all pairs.

ideas.name: Minimise the largest edge on a path
ideas.summary: Use the path's maximum edge as its cost in Dijkstra, or add edges in sorted order until the ends connect.

ideas.name: Minimum spanning tree (Kruskal or Prim)
ideas.summary: Take edges from cheapest up, skipping any that would close a cycle, until all nodes are joined.

ideas.name: Tarjan low-link: bridges and strongly connected parts
ideas.summary: Track each node's DFS entry time and the earliest time reachable from its subtree to find bridges and SCCs.

ideas.name: 0-1 BFS with a deque
ideas.summary: When edges cost 0 or 1, push 0-edges to the front and 1-edges to the back of a deque instead of using a heap.

ideas.name: Fill k buckets
ideas.summary: Put each item into one of k buckets, pruning by capacity and by skipping buckets in the same state.

ideas.name: Unbounded knapsack
ideas.summary: For each amount, try every coin as the last one used; coins may be reused.

ideas.name: DP over grid paths
ideas.summary: Each cell's value comes from the cell above and the cell to the left, and one row of memory is enough.

ideas.name: Best subarray ending here (Kadane)
ideas.summary: The best subarray ending at i either extends the one ending at i-1 or starts fresh at i.

ideas.name: 0/1 knapsack and subset sum
ideas.summary: Process items one at a time and update reachable sums from high to low so each item is used once.

ideas.name: Two-sequence DP (LCS)
ideas.summary: dp[i][j] answers the question for the first i items of one sequence and the first j of the other.

ideas.name: Longest increasing subsequence
ideas.summary: dp[i] is the longest increasing run that ends at i, built from every earlier smaller item.

ideas.name: Partition DP: choose the last segment
ideas.summary: dp[i] tries every length for the final segment ending at i and adds the best answer before it.

ideas.name: State-machine DP
ideas.summary: Keep one DP value per state (holding, not holding, cooling down) and move between states each day.

ideas.name: Take-or-skip DP
ideas.summary: At each item, the best is either skipping it or taking it plus the best that is compatible with taking it.

ideas.name: Count ways DP
ideas.summary: The number of ways to reach i is the sum of the ways of the states that lead to i, often taken mod 1e9+7.

ideas.name: DP over prefixes with a dictionary
ideas.summary: Prefix i is breakable if some earlier breakable prefix j is followed by a dictionary word s[j:i].

ideas.name: DP plus binary search over earlier items
ideas.summary: Sort by end time; dp[i] takes job i plus the best dp at the last job that ends before it starts, found by binary search.

ideas.name: Monotonic deque to speed up a window DP
ideas.summary: When dp[i] needs the best dp value in a sliding window, keep that window's candidates in a monotonic deque.

ideas.name: Speed up DP transitions with prefix sums
ideas.summary: When dp[i] sums a range of the previous row, keep that row's prefix sums so each transition is O(1).

ideas.name: Probability and expected-value DP
ideas.summary: Spread probability from each state to the states it can move to, step by step.

ideas.name: Enumerate the submasks of a mask
ideas.summary: Loop sub = (sub - 1) & mask to visit every subset of a mask; over all masks this costs 3^n.

ideas.name: Bitmask DP over (visited set, last node)
ideas.summary: The state is which nodes are visited and where you are now, as in the travelling salesman DP.

ideas.name: KMP prefix function
ideas.summary: For each prefix, store the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix, so a mismatch never re-reads text.

ideas.name: Manacher's algorithm for all palindromes
ideas.summary: Reuse the mirror image inside the rightmost palindrome found so far to get every centre's radius in O(n).

ideas.name: Binary search on length with rolling hashes
ideas.summary: If a repeated substring of length L exists, one of length L-1 does too, so binary search L and test with hashes.

ideas.name: Suffix array and LCP
ideas.summary: Sort all suffixes; neighbours in that order share the longest prefixes, which answers many substring questions.

ideas.name: Search a trie with DFS and wildcards
ideas.summary: On a wildcard, try every child; on a letter, follow one child.

ideas.name: Nim sums and Sprague–Grundy numbers
ideas.summary: A sum of games is lost exactly when the XOR of the parts' Grundy numbers (the mex of their moves) is zero.

ideas.name: Matrix exponentiation for linear recurrences
ideas.summary: Write one DP step as a matrix and raise it to the n-th power by squaring, so n steps cost O(k^3 log n).

ideas.name: Disjoint intervals in a sorted map
ideas.summary: Store non-overlapping intervals keyed by start, and merge with the neighbours found by floor and ceiling.

ideas.name: LFU cache with frequency buckets
ideas.summary: Keep one recency list per use count and track the minimum count, so the least-used, oldest key is evicted in O(1).

ideas.name: Square-root decomposition
ideas.summary: Handle small steps or blocks with a precomputed table and large ones by brute force, splitting the work at about sqrt(n).

ideas.name: Sweep plus segment tree for areas
ideas.summary: Sweep one axis and keep the covered length of the other axis in a segment tree over compressed coordinates.

ideas.name: Graphs where each node has one out-edge
ideas.summary: With one out-edge per node, the graph is cycles with trees hanging into them; walk with timestamps to find cycles.

ideas.name: Peel leaves layer by layer
ideas.summary: Remove all current leaves in rounds, like a BFS from the outside, until the centre remains.

ideas.name: Derive the graph from ordering constraints
ideas.summary: Turn each 'a comes before b' fact into an edge, then topologically sort the letters or items.

ideas.name: Bipartite matching and max flow
ideas.summary: Repeatedly find an augmenting path (alternating free and matched edges, or residual capacity) and push along it; the largest flow equals the smallest cut.

ideas.name: Edit distance
ideas.summary: Each cell takes the cheapest of insert, delete or replace from the three neighbouring cells.

ideas.name: LIS in O(n log n) with tails
ideas.summary: Keep the smallest possible tail for each length and place each new item by binary search.

ideas.name: DP over a DAG in topological order
ideas.summary: When dependencies form a DAG, compute each node's value after all of its predecessors, by topo order or memoised DFS.

ideas.name: Interval DP over ranges [i, j]
ideas.summary: Solve every range from short to long, building each range from slightly shorter ones.

ideas.name: Row-by-row DP with a row mask
ideas.summary: Process a grid row by row and keep the previous row's choices as a bitmask in the state.

ideas.name: Tree DP with per-node states
ideas.summary: Each node returns the best value for each of its states (such as taken or not), computed from its children.

ideas.name: Aho–Corasick for many patterns
ideas.summary: Add KMP-style failure links to a trie of all patterns, so one pass over the text finds every pattern.

ideas.name: Trie-guided backtracking on a grid
ideas.summary: Walk the grid and the trie together, stopping as soon as the path is no prefix of any word.

ideas.name: Pattern-matching DP (wildcards, regex)
ideas.summary: Match text against a pattern cell by cell, where '*' may match nothing or one more character.

ideas.name: Rerooting DP
ideas.summary: Compute the answer for one root, then move the root across each edge and adjust the answer in O(1).

ideas.name: Interval DP with a split point
ideas.summary: For range [i, j], try every split k and combine [i, k] and [k, j] plus the cost of the split.

ideas.name: Next permutation: last rise, swap, reverse
ideas.summary: Find the last place where the order goes up, swap it with the next larger item on its right, then reverse the tail.

ideas.name: Two competing candidates (duel pointers)
ideas.summary: Keep two candidate start positions, compare them letter by letter, and drop the loser together with the part it already beat.

ideas.name: Switch lists so two pointers walk equal distance
ideas.summary: When a pointer reaches the end of its list it jumps to the other list's head, so both pointers meet after walking the same distance.

ideas.name: Remember the last position of an event
ideas.summary: Store the last index where something happened, so each new position can be measured or counted against it in constant time.

ideas.name: The median minimizes total distance
ideas.summary: To make all items equal at the least total distance, move them all to the median, which you find after sorting.

ideas.name: Sort, then take the best items until full
ideas.summary: Sort by the best key, then take items one by one until the budget or the limit is used up.

ideas.name: Sort both lists and pair them in order
ideas.summary: The best way to pair two lists is to sort both and match the i-th item of one with the i-th item of the other.

ideas.name: Greedy from the leftmost digit or letter
ideas.summary: The leftmost position changes the result most, so fix it first and change the first place where a change helps.

ideas.name: Count first, then use values in a greedy order
ideas.summary: Count how often each value appears, then use values in a good order, such as the smallest first or the rarest first.

ideas.name: Work backward from the end result
ideas.summary: Undo the steps starting from the target: each backward step is forced or much simpler than the forward choice.

ideas.name: Few distinct AND / OR / GCD values over subarrays
ideas.summary: As a subarray grows, its AND, OR or GCD changes only about log times, so keep the short list of distinct values for each end.

ideas.name: Reachability by gcd (Bezout)
ideas.summary: Adding and subtracting multiples of a and b gives exactly the multiples of gcd(a, b), so reachability becomes a gcd test.

ideas.name: Closest pair by divide and conquer
ideas.summary: Split the points by x, solve both halves, then check only the thin strip around the dividing line.

ideas.name: Smallest enclosing circle
ideas.summary: Add points in random order; when a point falls outside the circle, rebuild the circle with that point on its edge.

ideas.name: Fast polynomial multiplication (FFT)
ideas.summary: Multiplying polynomials is a convolution; the FFT turns it into pointwise products in O(n log n).

ideas.name: Ask smart questions to a hidden judge
ideas.summary: When you may only ask a judge a few questions, choose queries that remove many candidates at once and then update what is still possible.

ideas.name: Longest path in a tree (diameter)
ideas.summary: The longest path through a node joins its two deepest branches, so each node returns its depth and updates a global best.

ideas.name: BFS shortest paths with parent lists
ideas.summary: Run BFS to get distances and parent lists, then walk back from the target to list every shortest path.

ideas.name: Solve a game backward from its end states
ideas.summary: Mark the states with a known result, then push wins and losses backward through the state graph, counting moves left.

ideas.name: DP or merging driven by a monotonic stack
ideas.summary: Keep a monotonic stack so the best earlier state, or the cheapest merge partner, is found in amortized constant time.

ideas.name: DP with an extra counter in the state
ideas.summary: Add a small counter, such as trades used, groups formed or switches left, to the DP state next to the last choice.

ideas.name: String DP with fast piece comparison
ideas.summary: Let a DP over positions use a fast string comparison, such as a hash or an LCP table, to decide which cuts are allowed.

ideas.name: Search the minimum of a convex function
ideas.summary: A convex cost has one lowest point: compare the cost at m and m+1, or use ternary search, to know which side to keep.

ideas.name: Walk down a segment tree to the first fit
ideas.summary: Store a summary such as the maximum in each node, then walk down from the root to the first position that fits.

ideas.name: DP sped up by a Fenwick or segment tree
ideas.summary: Speed up a DP that needs the best earlier value with a smaller key by keeping those values in a Fenwick or segment tree.

ideas.name: SQL window functions
ideas.summary: Window functions such as LAG, RANK and ROW_NUMBER compare a row with its neighbours or rank it inside a group without collapsing rows.

ideas.name: SQL string and date functions
ideas.summary: Built-in string, regex and date functions split, format or extract parts of a value, so cleaning text needs no loop.

ideas.name: Difference array over candidate answers
ideas.summary: For every pair, add to the range of target values that cost 0, 1 or 2 changes, then scan the difference array for the best target.

families.name: Arrays, hashing & sorting
families.description: One pass with running state, hash sets and maps, counting, sorting as a tool, and divide-and-conquer counting.

families.name: Prefix sums, difference arrays & sweeps
families.description: Precomputed running totals for range questions, range updates with difference arrays, and line sweeps over sorted events.

families.name: Two pointers & sliding windows
families.description: Two indexes that only move forward: from both ends, read/write, merging, and fixed or variable windows.

families.name: Stacks, queues, monotonic structures & linked lists
families.description: Last-in first-out matching and parsing, queues, monotonic stacks and deques, and pointer work on linked lists.

families.name: Binary search
families.description: Halving a sorted range or an answer space with a monotone yes/no test, including rotated arrays, matrices and k-th values.

families.name: Trees & binary search trees
families.description: Recursion on trees, traversal orders, values passed up or down, BST order, construction and serialization.

families.name: Graph traversal, topological sort & union–find
families.description: Adjacency lists, DFS and BFS on graphs and grids, states as nodes, cycle checks, topological order and disjoint sets.

families.name: Shortest paths & advanced graphs
families.description: Weighted shortest paths, spanning trees, Euler paths, bridges, matching, and tree queries with binary lifting.

families.name: Heaps, greedy & intervals
families.description: Priority queues, top-k and k-way merge, greedy choices with exchange arguments, interval scheduling and merging.

families.name: Recursion & backtracking
families.description: Exhaustive search by recursion: subsets, combinations, permutations, placement puzzles and pruning.

families.name: Dynamic programming 1: linear, knapsack, grid & sequences
families.description: Memoised recursion and tables over one index, knapsacks, grid paths, two-sequence DP and LIS.

families.name: Dynamic programming 2: interval, tree, bitmask, digit & games
families.description: DP over ranges, trees, subsets and digits, game and probability DP, and faster transitions (deque, prefix sums, binary search).

families.name: Strings: processing, parsing, tries & matching
families.description: Character scanning and building, tokenising, state machines, palindromes, tries, KMP, Z, rolling hashes and suffix structures.

families.name: Math: number theory, combinatorics, geometry, probability & games
families.description: Digits and bases, modular arithmetic, primes and GCD, counting formulas, geometry, randomness and combinatorial games.

families.name: Bit manipulation
families.description: Bitwise operators, XOR tricks, per-bit counting, bitmasks as sets, prefix XOR and binary tries.

families.name: Design & range data structures
families.description: Classes with required time bounds: caches, iterators, versioned maps, ordered sets, segment and Fenwick trees.

families.name: Simulation & matrices
families.description: Following the rules step by step, grid indexing and direction arrays, matrix transforms, cycles in states.

families.name: Platform topics: JavaScript, pandas/SQL & concurrency
families.description: Closures, promises and timers in JavaScript, table operations in pandas/SQL, and thread coordination.
